editorial.headline: Coffee Farming That Is Nationally Open and Bali-Clear
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01271 covers the full coffee-farming cycle, from land preparation and seed work through cultivation, harvest, and integrated post-harvest activity.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01271 is the coffee-farming code, not a cafe, trading, roasting, or hospitality label.** Its scope is agricultural and begins in the field: land preparation, sowing, nursery work, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one connected farming sequence. The record also brings coffee seed production into the same field of view, through nursery and seed activities for beverage crops. In plain English, this is the code for cultivating coffee as an agricultural activity, including the practical upstream work needed to raise the plant and bring the crop through harvest.

That breadth matters because it makes the code useful for operators whose real business is coffee production rather than merely handling coffee as a product. A founder registering under this activity is describing the cultivation system itself: preparing land, developing seedlings, planting coffee, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling the immediate post-harvest work that belongs to the same farming chain. The slim record does not add processing thresholds, special licensing language, land-size rules, tax treatment, or capital figures, so the clean reading stays close to the activity description: agriculture first, with coffee as the crop and the farming sequence as the core.

The scale position is unusually straightforward. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the code is not confined, in the record, to a single business size band. A small grower, a growing medium enterprise, or a large-scale operator can all sit within the same activity description, provided the registered business is genuinely performing the coffee-farming work described. The important editorial distinction is that scale availability is not the same thing as an invented permission package. The record says which scales are open; it does not state extra conditions beyond the listed activity scope and the stated foreign-investment position.

For foreign ownership, the national picture is clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap in the record, so the national reading is that this activity can be foreign-owned up to the stated ceiling. The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason than many founders expect. The Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, yet this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is simple: on the record provided, a foreign-owned company can register this coffee-farming activity in Bali today, because the Bali moratorium does not block it.
